issues.kind: example contradicts law 1 (5) with law 2 (a) and law 3
issues.claim: The way-and-channel table's row (b), its gates cell (ARCHITECTURE.md l. 2914): 'such a crossing of the trace is moved along the deck to the nearest crossing clear of the strip (`bend.raised.underSpan`, its wall form)'; row W2's last column (l. 3341): 'a gate it makes for a ground way where law 1 (5) bars one placed along that way clear of the strip, the stretch bent through it'. Law 1 (5) (l. 2724-2725) admits a gate in an aqueduct's over crossing wherever every span over its footprint clears its top; law 2 (a) (l. 2803-2813) moves what the op lays or places no further than the nearest clear points and law 3 (l. 2846-2852) picks the least displacement, so under an aqueduct whose arch over the drawn crossing does not clear the gate the laws put the moved crossing under the nearest arch that does (inside the strip), and along W2's way they stop the gate where no span over its footprint fails to clear it (possibly in the strip's margin). The fix pass conformed §7.1's bend.raised.underSpan row (l. 11340: 'its crossing of a trace to the nearest at which §2.7's laws admit its gate'), V09's line and T110-2 (5)'s second run (l. 19476-19479: 'moved along the deck to the nearest crossing at which §2.7's laws admit its gate'); these two cells kept the pre-J149 words. A build from row (b) fails T110-2 (5)'s second run; the laws govern (J146): minor.
issues.required_change: (model) Row (b)'s gates cell: "such a crossing of the trace is moved along the deck to the nearest crossing clear of the strip (`bend.raised.underSpan`, its wall form)" → "such a crossing of the trace is moved along the deck to the nearest crossing at which these laws admit its gate (law 1 (5), law 3; `bend.raised.underSpan`, its wall form)". Row W2's last column: "a gate it makes for a ground way where law 1 (5) bars one placed along that way clear of the strip, the stretch bent through it" → "a gate it makes for a ground way where law 1 (5) bars one placed along that way at the nearest point these laws admit it (law 2 (a), law 3), the stretch bent through it".

issues.claim: *beneath*'s *Where the line crosses* (l. 3060-3063): 'over where its channel runs above the wall's top — under a span that clears the wall's top, or through a `cleared` support's ring (open ground: both its spans fallen, C5), never through a standing support'; the bent-group sentence's lawful crossing (l. 3184-3186), to which (i) moves every unlawful crossing: 'under a span that clears it or through a `cleared` support's ring (open ground, C5)'. Law 1 (2) (l. 2705-2712) reads the levels 'from the records, each span's soffit standing or fallen' and admits over only with 'every span above the band clearing the wall's top', 'a crossing that fits neither form' unlawful. A `cleared` support's two spans have fallen (C5, l. 3271-3272) and a band wider than the ring lies under them; where either's recorded soffit is below the wall's top a band through the ring fits neither form. The fix pass widened *beneath*'s own impassables for exactly this case (l. 3080-3082: 'each widened so that the band's half at most touches the ring or that strip'; adjudication-r7v M8's note), but not the two sentences that define the lawful crossing a hand stroke, VS3's palisade and a re-section take. A move to such a ring breaks law 1 (2) and fails §5.3's law-1 row (l. 9940) at the commit, so a wrong build is caught: minor.
issues.required_change: (model) *Where the line crosses*: "or through a `cleared` support's ring (open ground: both its spans fallen, C5)," → "or through a `cleared` support's ring (open ground: both its spans fallen, C5) where every span above the band, standing or fallen, clears that top,". The bent-group sentence: "under a span that clears it or through a `cleared` support's ring (open ground, C5)," → "under a span that clears it or through a `cleared` support's ring (open ground, C5) where every span above its band, standing or fallen, clears it,".

issues.claim: The fixed-place sentence, *A raised way created after the wall* (l. 3259-3262): 'a road deck keeps each outside its zone and an aqueduct each out of its strip but under arches that clear it, and either keeps each off its ramps, stairs and feet ... (law 1 (4), (6))'; *beneath*'s *No gate and no tower* (l. 3155-3159): 'A gate or tower whose place the wall's own law fixes — a river's water gate, an anchor's tower, a harbour-mouth chain, a castle's town-side gate and vertex towers ... — never moves along: whichever is laid later keeps it out of a road deck's zone, and out of an aqueduct's strip but under arches that clear it'. An anchor ends its stretch's line on its barrier (*fixed place*, l. 2627-2629) and law 1 (4) (l. 2721-2723) lets a band lie in a raised way's strip 'only to cross its deck line — entering on one long side, leaving by the other', so no anchor lies in an aqueduct's strip whatever its arches clear: Part L's correction 7 (adjudication-r7.md l. 699: 'never an anchor (law 1 (4) ...)'), the restated veto list's item 7 (l. 742: 'an anchor, which ends its wall's line, under none') and Part P's PRB7F-GEN-08 (l. 3687) say so, and T110-2 (1)'s variant (l. 19307-19310: 'the anchor lies outside its under-deck strip and the water gate and the weld vertex outside it save under an arch that clears them') and T110-2 (4)'s refusal (l. 19461-19463) run it. The two sentences, the second naming the anchor's tower, admit it under a clearing arch; §5.3's law-1 row catches a build from them: minor.
issues.required_change: (model) The fixed-place sentence: "and an aqueduct each out of its strip but under arches that clear it," → "and an aqueduct each out of its strip but under arches that clear it, an anchor out of it always (law 1 (4)),". *No gate and no tower*: "and out of an aqueduct's strip but under arches that clear it (law 1 (6); the fixed-place sentence)" → "and out of an aqueduct's strip but under arches that clear it, an anchor's tower out of it always (law 1 (4), (6); the fixed-place sentence)".

issues.kind: VALID CHOICE (J151): two readings of law 1 (5), every outcome lawful
issues.claim: Law 1 (5) (l. 2724-2725): 'no gate's, postern's or tower's footprint lies in a strip, under a standing span or a fallen one, but in an aqueduct's crossing law 1 (2) reads over whose every span over it clears its top, never on a support's ring'. The terms (l. 2618-2619) define 'a standing support one whose `state` is absent or `ruined`; a `cleared` one's ring is open ground', law 1 (2)'s over form bars only a 'standing support in the band', and *Where the line crosses* lets a band pass 'through a `cleared` support's ring'. Law 1 (5) names no state, so a gate, postern or tower whose footprint falls on a `cleared` support's ring in an over crossing whose spans clear it is (a) lawful (the ring open ground) or (b) barred (every support's ring) — S7's tower by spacing, S5a's pin, a placeGate or a slid gate there standing in (a), moved along the trace to the nearest lawful point in (b) (law 2 (a), law 3). Each keeps law 1 as it reads it and every owner rule (J148: no standing gate or tower moved; J149: a gate under a clearing arch); a later hand repair of that support raises a new part whose supports (1)-(5) place off the band (C10, l. 3291-3296) and repairRaised raises only a `ruined` part (V06 l. 726), so neither reading leaves a later op without an outcome; no named test places a footprint on a `cleared` ring (the state sweep asserts only 'no gate's or tower's footprint in the under-deck strip but where §2.7's laws, law 1 (5), admit one', l. 19278-19279).
issues.required_change: VALID CHOICE (J151): fix-list.md's builders' choices list "§2.7's laws, law 1 (5)'s 'never on a support's ring' — read of every support (a gate, postern or tower never on a `cleared` support's ring, moved along the trace to the nearest lawful point, law 2 (a), law 3) or of a standing one (a `cleared` ring open ground, the footprint lawful there in an over crossing whose spans clear it)"; the builder picks one. No design text changes.

issues.kind: VALID CHOICE (J151): two examples give two counts
issues.claim: Row W14's last column (l. 3353): 'at an epoch each crossing counted in `walls.raisedCrossings`'; the bent-group sentence (l. 3212-3214), which W14's C2 makes the re-sectioned run's rule: 'at an epoch the stretch's crossings of the deck line are counted in `walls.raisedCrossings` as *Reported* says'; *Reported* (l. 3164-3168): 'once per crossing of a trace laid after a raised way'; *Paths and tests* (l. 3328-3330): 'count only a trace laid after a raised way crossing its deck line'; V06 §2.10's field (V06 l. 756): 'crossings of a trace this epoch laid or re-sectioned ..., counted as the crossing table's *Reported* says'. A re-section keeps its line's order (*Order*, l. 2683-2684), so a palisade an aqueduct was created across (C1, *over the band*) — the carried-down CITY ring a village REPLACEMENT rebuilds in stone among them (T-V7-48) — is (a) counted at the REPLACEMENT's epoch (W14; V06's 'or re-sectioned') or (b) not counted (*Reported*: no trace laid after the raised way). No law-1 invariant, no clause of the check and no named test reads the count (T-V6-47 counts new circuits and contractions, V06 l. 4220; T-V7-48's REPLACEMENT clauses count nothing).
issues.required_change: VALID CHOICE (J151): fix-list.md's builders' choices list "§2.7's crossing table, row W14 at an epoch: a run re-sectioned on a trace older than the raised way it crosses — each crossing counted in `walls.raisedCrossings` at the re-section's epoch (W14; V06 §2.10's 'laid or re-sectioned'), or counted only where the run was laid after the raised way (*Reported*)"; the builder picks one. No design text changes.
